'''Peter Sheridan Dodds''' is an Australian [[Applied mathematician|applied Mathematician]]. He is the director of the [[Vermont Complex Systems Institute]] and Professor at the [[University of Vermont]]'s Department of Mathematics and Statistics.  He has collaborated in several researches related to big data problems in areas as [[language]], [[Narrative|stories]], [[sociotechnical systems]], [[Complex system|complex systems]], [[Earth science]], [[biology]], and [[ecology]]. With [[Chris Danforth]], he co-runs the [[Computational Story Lab]], the [[MassMutual Center of Excellence in Complex Systems and Data Science]], and together, they developed the [[hedonometer]].<ref name="vcs">{{cite web |title=Peter Dodds |url=https://vermontcomplexsystems.org/people/core-team/peterdodds |website=Vermont Complex Systems |access-date=15 November 2020}}</ref><ref name="plos">{{cite web |title=Science of Stories Collection |url=https://everyone.plos.org/2020/02/03/science-of-stories-collection/ |website=PlOS |date=3 February 2020 |access-date=15 November 2020}}</ref>

Recent research directed by Dodds has been commented on in ''[[The New York Times]]'', ''[[Smithsonian Magazine]]'', and other media. In October 2020, the Hedonometor tool created by Dodds and his Danforth analyzed the sentiment of people through their tweets to identify May 31 as the saddest day recorded.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schwartz |first1=Casey |title=Is Everybody Doing... OK? Let's Ask Social Media |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/10/12/style/self-care/social-media-.html?smid=tw-nytimes&smtyp=cur |access-date=15 November 2020 |work=The New York Times |date=12 October 2020 |ref=nyt}}</ref><ref name="smag">{{cite web |last1=McGreevy |first1=Nora |title=New Research Suggests We're Living in Historically Unhappy Times |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/new-research-suggests-were-living-historically-unhappy-times-180975123/ |website=Smithsonian Magazine |access-date=15 November 2020}}</ref>

In Dodds's early career, from 2002 to 2007, he was a frequent collaborator of [[Duncan J. Watts]].

In 2016, Dodds collaborated with Danforth and Mark Ibrahim on writing about [[Wikipedia philosophy phenomenon|the phenomenon]] where [[Wikipedia]] articles are connected by "[[Philosophy]]".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Collins |first=Nathan |date=9 May 2016 |title=All Wikipedia Roads Lead to Philosophy, but Some of Them Go Through Southeast Europe First |url=https://psmag.com/news/all-wikipedia-roads-lead-to-philosophy-but-some-of-them-go-through-southeast-europe-first/ |access-date=30 June 2025 |work=[[Pacific Standard]]}}</ref>

In 2023, as part of a group of researchers in the Vermont Complex Systems Institute, he helped win a National Science Foundation award to study the science of stories. This 5-year grant was called The Science of Online Corpora, Knowledge, and Stories (SOCKS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=UVM Earns $20M Research Grant to ‘Harness the Data Revolution’ |url=https://www.uvm.edu/uvmnews/news/uvm-earns-20m-research-grant-harness-data-revolution |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=www.uvm.edu |language=en}}</ref>
